requirement:
The harness instructs the model to finish by calling
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission.mcp`.
rationale:
structural: The subject text of `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission` is one sentence: "The harness instructs the model to finish by calling `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission.mcp`." It only describes observable behavior. The model is told, in the prompt or instructions, to end by calling the submission tool. It names no library, type, signature, field, algorithm or delegation interface.

I considered whether any clause could be a structural obligation. I tried an alternative that behaves the same way but changes how the instruction is built. For example, the instruction text could come from a constant, a template, a function, or a different module. The model would still be told to finish by calling `submit_result`, so the text is still satisfied. How the instruction is produced is therefore discretionary.

The `schemars` derivation, the one-argument tool shape, and the conversation ending on acceptance belong to the cited `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission.mcp` and `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission.acceptance`. Those are cited as context, not refined here, and the task limits this review to the subject's own text. No implementation roots were supplied, and none is needed for a requirement that states only behavior.

behavioral: The subject has one behavioral obligation: the harness instructs the model to finish by calling `submit_result`. It cites `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission.mcp`, which defines the tool's shape, so I also checked that the tests apply that shape.

The instruction is asserted in three places:
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/configured.rs#mod[tests]/fn[supplied_openai_backend_runs_independent_calls_against_a_local_transport]` checks that the request input of every one of the four requests contains "Finish by calling submit_result".
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/configured.rs#mod[tests]/fn[supplied_ollama_backend_delivers_tools_and_results_over_native_chat]` checks that the messages contain it on both turns.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[assistant_text_and_provider_failure_cannot_become_typed_results]` checks that the first request's chat history contains it.

These tests cover the OpenAI and Ollama backends and the generic `ToolAgent` path. They assert on the actual request content sent to the provider, so an omitted or altered instruction would fail them.

The cited tool contract is also checked.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[default_tool_accepts_scalar_results_and_keeps_the_exact_prefix]` checks that `submit_result` is offered and that its result schema is boolean.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[typed_submission_references_resolve]` checks that `required` is `["result"]`, that `additionalProperties` is false and that there is exactly one property.
- The OpenAI and Ollama tests check that `required` is `["result"]`.

All of these tests carry `{test}` references to the subject. I found no unmarked relevant tests and no untested obligation.
